overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law. Entering executive session under Purpose 3 was appropriate because the Board still had a litigating position to protect in the pending suits, even though it was not a named party in several.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board convened in executive session on February 1 without a proper Purpose 3 litigation basis, since it was not a named party in several of the cases discussed.
allegations.key_passage: A public body that is not a named party in litigation may still have a litigating position to protect where such body undertakes legal or financial responsibilities in the litigation and is "an active participant in litigation strategy."
